contrastiveness is a pragmatic notion, which is associated with a number of different phenomena.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contrastive topics, as a particular type of topics, are a kind of ‘incompletness’ markers, which are associated with a particular semantic-pragmatics effect.
contrastive topics operate on the speech act of assertion and are associated with the semantic/pragmatic notion of contrastiveness.
the semantic notion of contrastivity is not a simple one, and it is best to view it as a complex of different semantic/pragmatic phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contrastiveness is a pragmatic notion that operates on speech acts.
contrastive topics are not just a way of expressing a contrastive proposition.
contrastiveness is not a single notion, and that it has to be broken into at least three sub-notions, which can be called contrastive focus, contrastive topic, and contrastive polarity.
